text:
alex: quick check — running into odd behavior with flag inheritance for `reply_streaming`. Config I expect to win is model-level, but in e2e the project override seems to be winning. my mental model is model > route > project > org. anyone confirm?

maria: that's the canonical order we documented, yeah. but do you have any `force_off` or `force_on` semantics applied anywhere? those can short-circuit. :thinking_face:

alex: nope no explicit force flags. sample config:```yaml
feature_flags:
  reply_streaming:
    org: true
    project: false
    model: true
```
I expected model=true to win, but our test service returned false when hitting /v1/generate with the model header.

cheng: quick thought — are you hitting a route that has audience gating? we added a route-level canary recently that sets `project=false` for the 95% public audience and leaves model-level alone for internal 5%. If the request didn't carry the internal audience attr it would resolve to project=false.

alex: interesting. request didn't include `x-internal-audience`. so that would explain it. i guess i misread the precedence when audience gates exist.

devon: fwiw, we agreed offline that an explicit audience-scoped override should take precedence over generic model-level if the audience matches. so precedence becomes: explicit force flags > audience-scoped overrides (route/project/model scoped to audience) > scoped defaults. it's a bit nuanced.

maria: +1 — we should make that explicit in the flag resolution doc and add a unit test matrix. current ambiguity is causing repeated surprises.

samir: proposal: two guardrails — (1) `force_off` at any scope has absolute priority (prevents accidental enabling), (2) more-specific audience-scoped override wins over broader-scope general setting. e.g., model-level audience:true overrides project-level general:false.

alex: that would have avoided my confusion. can we also add a runtime lint that surfaces when a project-level override may unintentionally shadow model-level audience-specific flags? maybe a warning in console when saving a project override that reduces an existing narrower audience's enablement.

maria: good idea. i can file a short RFC+PR: add the lint + update docs + test matrix. devon can you review the PR when ready?

devon: yup, ping me — will do a quick pass. also suggest adding a tiny e2e that simulates requests with `x-audience: internal` vs absent to make the behavior explicit.

alex: pinging @deploy-bot — should we hold the canary rollout until we update the lint/docs? current canary is 5% internal audience enabled at model-level, project-level forces off for the rest.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled at 2026-04-02T15:00Z for route `reply` (5% internal). If you need to abort, run `/deploy abort 206789` or comment here.

cheng: I'd rather proceed but block the wider rollout until the lint/PR lands. small risk window.

samir: agreed — proceed with canary but set an auto-rollback if we observe unexpected false negatives for internal audience in the first 30 minutes. add a monitor that checks `flag_resolution` metric counts by audience.

maria: i'll open the RFC + PR today and add the test matrix. alex — can you add the failing e2e as a test case in the PR? that will make the regression obvious.

alex: yes, will add the test and link it. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: I created ticket #INF-4129 for the RFC + lint work and assigned it to maria.

alex: closing loop — last_message_ts update after deploy decision.
